subject: biology

moments.title: Gurdon's frog
moments.body: Gurdon transplants nuclei from intestinal cells into enucleated frog eggs and grows adult frogs. Differentiation is reversible. He shares the 2012 Nobel with Yamanaka.
moments.takeaway: Differentiated nuclei retain all genetic information — and can be reprogrammed.

moments.title: ES cells
moments.body: Mouse embryonic stem cells (1981) and human ES cells (1998) revolutionise developmental biology. But human ES use is ethically contested.
moments.takeaway: Pluripotent cells can be cultured indefinitely — but human ES cells require destroying embryos.

moments.title: Yamanaka factors
moments.body: Yamanaka and his student Takahashi screen 24 candidate genes and find that just four (Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, c-Myc) can reprogram adult fibroblasts to pluripotent stem cells. 2012 Nobel.
moments.takeaway: Adult cells can be reset to embryonic state with four genes.

moments.title: iPS in the clinic
moments.body: iPS-derived retinal pigment epithelial cells, dopaminergic neurons and CAR-T cells enter clinical trials. iPS cells are now standard in disease modelling and drug screening.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: iPS cells are used worldwide. CRISPR-edited iPS cells model genetic disease. Direct reprogramming bypasses pluripotency entirely.
now.open_questions: Can iPS-derived organoids replace organ transplants? Can we reverse cellular ageing safely?

reflection: Yamanaka's discovery removed the ethical objection to ES cells overnight. How often does technology dissolve ethical impasses?
